title: Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences Ltd - 543308 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 34.8% YoY to INR 1,075 crore, but EBITDA pre-Ind AS fell 33.5% to INR 131 crore as new hospitals dragged margins.
summary.overview: KIMS reported Q4 FY26 total revenue of INR 1,084 crore (+35.3% YoY, +8.1% QoQ) and EBITDA of INR 216 crore (+6.8% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 19.9% versus 25.3% a year ago. Management attributed the margin compression to roughly INR 32 crore of EBITDA erosion from newer units (in operation under one year), while mature units held about 28.5-29% margins. PAT fell to INR 33 crore from INR 106 crore a year ago. Management is raising about INR 1,500 crore via QIP to cut net debt, which it says has peaked at INR 3,000-plus crore, and targets net debt to EBITDA of 1-2x from about 1x-3x currently.

segments.name: Mature units
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 862 crore with EBITDA about INR 250 crore, a margin of roughly 28.5-29%. For FY26, mature units generated INR 3,335 crore revenue and about INR 956 crore EBITDA, about 29.5% margin.

segments.name: Newer units (under one year old)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 224 crore with EBITDA erosion of about INR 32 crore. For FY26, these units generated INR 597 crore revenue and about INR 128 crore EBITDA erosion.

segments.name: Mahadevapura (Bengaluru)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 49 crore and loss about INR 14 crore; management says it averages about INR 17 crore/month and targets INR 25-30 crore/month over 12 months.

segments.name: Electronic City / PES (Bengaluru)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 17 crore with loss about INR 25 crore; commissioned in December 2025. Management expects EBITDA-positive by end of FY27.

segments.name: Thane
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR 47 crore and loss about INR 5 crore. Management says Thane was EBITDA-neutral in March and April 2026, before adding doctors in May.

segments.name: Nashik
segments.commentary: Q4 loss about INR 1 crore. Still awaiting STAR, Medi Assist and GIPSA empanelment.

guidance_outlook: Telangana cluster EBITDA growth guided at about 10-12% in FY27, below historical rates due to Kondapur and Kompally.
Newer-unit combined losses in FY27 and FY28 expected to be less than half of the roughly INR 120-128 crore FY26 drag, subject to insurance empanelments.
Use about INR 1,000 crore of QIP proceeds to retire debt; remainder for losses and capex in existing facilities.

Palakkad (300-bed, acquired; consolidated) expected at INR 6.5-7 crore revenue in May 2026 with about 5% negative EBITDA, breakeven by June-July 2026, targeting INR 12-15 crore/month revenue over time.
Bangalore ARPOB to be modelled at INR 75,000 annually; Andhra ARPOB at about INR 26,000-27,000.
Bengaluru occupancy expected at 35-40% by end of FY27 on full bed capacity.
Kondapur move to new 800-bed facility from first week of June 2026; Phase 1 of 400-500 beds; INR 50-75 crore further capex deferred to FY28-FY29.
capex_capacity: New Kondapur (Hyderabad) 800-bed hospital; shift from old facility starting first week of June 2026, with a one-month transition and old facility possibly running 2-3 months more.
Phase 1 of Kondapur to open at 400-500 beds; remaining 300 beds to be commissioned as occupancy rises.

Expansions in FY26: Kompally (Hyderabad), two in Guntur, Thane and Sangli (Maharashtra), Mahadevapura and Electronic City (Bengaluru), Kollam (Kerala), and fertility centres in Hyderabad and Guntur. KIMS Cuddles mother-and-child unit opened in Nellore; cancer block opened in Ongole.

Greenfield projects planned in Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu (one hospital), with continued expansion in Andhra and Telangana; these take 3-5 years to commission. Secunderabad expansion expected within 18 months.
Project funding norm: about 40% equity and 65% debt. Doctor participation typically 3-5% of equity; the model remains open.
demand_pricing: Average revenue per operating bed rose 13.7% YoY and 1.7% QoQ in Q4; average revenue per patient up 14% YoY and 3.5% QoQ.
IP volumes up 17.9% YoY and 4% QoQ; OP volumes up 30.1% YoY and 4.1% QoQ in Q4. FY26 IP volumes +15.4%, OP +25.4%.
Maharashtra Q4 occupancy at 60.5% (FY26 about 52.1%), which management calls the new base.
Hyderabad is the most competitive market; 4-5 hospitals commissioned in the last year. Management reports losing only one or two doctors, with no material attrition.
Insurance empanelment delays (new GIC common empanelment process and volume of new hospitals) are the main ramp-up constraint for new units.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise a INR 1,500 crore QIP after saying debt had peaked, and are new expansion plans firm?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt is near INR 3,000-plus crore and the QIP will retire debt, with cash flow then funding 3-5 year greenfield projects. Expansion plans are still being explored; 400-500 beds of small acquisitions may come in the next two quarters, all in home markets.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress on insurance empanelment for the new hospitals?
qa_highlights.answer: Nashik still needs STAR, Medi Assist and GIPSA. Thane has GIPSA, with Medi Assist and STAR nearly done, covering about 70% of insurance volume. Bangalore needs 3-4 more months. Confusion from the new GIC common-empanelment process caused the delays.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ARPOB and occupancy run-rates for Bangalore and Andhra Pradesh for modelling?
qa_highlights.answer: Bangalore ARPOB of about INR 85,000 for FY26 but management says to model INR 75,000. Andhra at about INR 26,000-27,000 in Q3 and Q4. Bengaluru occupancy expected 35-40% by end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kondapur capex and phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: The 800-bed Kondapur facility is almost fully capex-complete, with INR 50-75 crore left for two additional floors in FY28-FY29. Phase 1 covers 400-500 beds. Transition cost is expected to be about INR 15-25 crore, based on the Sunshine move precedent.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt outlook for FY27 after the QIP?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,000 crore of debt to be retired from QIP proceeds. The balance covers losses at new hospitals and capex in existing facilities.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA growth is expected for the Telangana cluster in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Telangana cluster EBITDA growth of about 10-12% in FY27, below historical levels because of the Kondapur and Kompally commissioning.

risks_watch: Insurance empanelment delays at Nashik, Thane and Bangalore hospitals, which management says limit ramp-up.
Margin dilution from new units: cluster-level margins, not company-level, are the guided metric; Q4 company margin was 19.9%.
Leverage: management targets net debt/EBITDA of 1-2x; the call says the current ratio is about 1x-3x (ambiguous). The QIP is about INR 1,500 crore.
Q4 PAT of INR 33 crore and EPS decline of 37.2% in FY26, with management acknowledging ROE and ROCE have fallen.
Geopolitical and macro risk: management cited the Gulf war and a government austerity appeal.
Competition for doctors in Hyderabad; possible common-empanelment initiative by IRDAI/GIC, which management declined to comment on.
Inconsistencies in disclosures: bed-addition plan changed without a timeline; management said the update would come next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating metrics and cluster-level margin trajectory, but cautious on near-term profitability, acknowledging that new-unit losses and insurance empanelment delays will persist. Management was evasive on forward-looking growth numbers and on the common-empanelment policy.
key_quotes: Expansion has no meaning without clinical excellence and excellence is incomplete without empathy.
As long as we are able to grow that on a quarter-on-quarter basis, that is the direction we should look at.
Right now, the only challenge I see is the insurance empanelment.
